title: Goldman Sachs Upgrades India to Overweight, Sets End-2027 Nifty Target of 28,500
excerpt: The bank expects 15 percent earnings growth in each of the next two years and calls India an AI diversifier after an unprecedented 83-percentage-point underperformance against the region.
body:
• Goldman Sachs upgraded Indian equities to overweight in its Asia-Pacific portfolio strategy on November 18 and set a Nifty target of 28,500 by end-2027, implying roughly 12 percent upside from current levels, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.
  • The target rests on Goldman's expectation of Nifty earnings-per-share growth of 15 percent in both 2027 and 2028 — a forecast, not a result — and on foreign ownership having fallen to a decade-plus low.
  • Goldman is overweight banks, defence, utilities, telecom and internet stocks, newly overweight industrials, and underweight IT services and healthcare.
  • The same report expects inflation of 5.7 percent in 2027 and 75 basis points of Reserve Bank tightening — the clearest risk to its own call.

Goldman Sachs has upgraded India to overweight in its Asia-Pacific portfolio strategy, setting a Nifty target of 28,500 by end-2027, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. "We raised India to overweight on its appeal as an AI diversifier. We expect the NIFTY to reach 28,500 by end-2027, driven by 15% earnings growth," the bank said in its report, according to ANI. The target implies roughly 12 percent upside from current levels.

Why now: the underperformance has been extreme

The upgrade is a mean-reversion call built on how far India has fallen behind. India's peak-to-trough underperformance reached 83 percentage points between mid-2024 and late-2026 against the MSCI Asia Pacific ex-Japan index — unprecedented, Goldman said. In the two prior instances of back-to-back annual underperformance, Indian equities subsequently outperformed the region by 38 percentage points in the following year. After a cumulative foreign investor selloff of $64 billion between 2024 and 2026, foreign ownership of Indian equities has fallen to a decade-plus low; since mid-October, India has received the largest share of foreign inflows within the emerging-markets pack.

The earnings evidence

Corporate earnings have beaten consensus estimates for five consecutive quarters. MSCI India companies excluding commodities posted 16 percent profit growth and 21 percent revenue growth in the third quarter, both multi-year highs, and Goldman forecasts Nifty earnings-per-share growth of 15 percent in both 2027 and 2028 — the strongest in the region outside South Korea and Taiwan. "With earnings growth slowing globally as AI capex peaks, India's durable growth appeal should come back," the bank said. Its economists expect real GDP growth of 7.9 percent in 2026, moderating to 7.2 percent in 2027, supported by a nascent private capital-expenditure cycle.

"We raised India to overweight on its appeal as an AI diversifier."

— Goldman Sachs, Asia-Pacific portfolio strategy report

Where Goldman would put money — and where it would not

On sector positioning, Goldman upgraded industrials to overweight on signs of a private capex recovery and retained overweight calls on banks, defence, utilities, telecom and internet. It remains underweight IT services and healthcare, citing potential earnings pressure as currency tailwinds recede and competition intensifies. For diaspora investors holding India exposure through funds or direct holdings, the practical read is sectoral: the bank's case is for domestic-facing cyclicals, not the export-heavy IT names that dominate many NRI portfolios.

The risks in the same report

Goldman's own economists are the call's main caution. They forecast above-consensus headline inflation of 5.7 percent year on year in 2027, driven by El Niño-related weather disruptions and elevated input costs, and expect the Reserve Bank of India to deliver a further 75 basis points of tightening, taking the repo rate to 6.25 percent by the second quarter of 2027. The bank also cautioned that crude oil prices could swing valuations either way: "Valuations could rise by 7-8% in our bull-case scenario, whereas they could de-rate 10-12% in the bear case," it said. On the currency, it forecasts USD/INR at 94, 95 and 96 over the three-, six- and twelve-month horizons. What to watch next: whether the earnings beats extend into a sixth quarter, and whether foreign inflows since mid-October hold once the AI trade stabilises.
